label: conj:q-oper-hecke
title: $q$-Opers are $q$-Hecke eigensheaves
html:
We explicitly construct q-Hecke eigensheaves from q-opers. Every q-oper (\mathcal{P}_{\check{G}_q}, abla_q) \in \mathrm{Op}_{\check{G}_q}(X) defines a point abla_q \in \mathrm{LocSys}_{\check{G}_q}(X). The q-Geometric Langlands equivalence (q-GL conjecture) maps the corresponding skyscraper sheaf \delta_{ abla_q} to a q-Hecke eigensheaf \mathcal{M}_{ abla_q} on \mathrm{Bun}_{G_q}(X):

  \mathcal{M}_{
abla_q} = \mathbb{L}_q^{-1}(\delta_{
abla_q}).

The eigenvalue q-local system is the q-oper connection itself. For each point x \in X and dominant weight \lambda, the Hecke action yields

  \mathbf{T}_{x,\lambda}^{(q)}(\mathcal{M}_{
abla_q})
  \simeq
  \mathcal{M}_{
abla_q} \otimes
  V_\lambda^{(q)}(
abla_q)_x.

The transversality condition defining the q-oper ensures that \mathcal{M}_{ abla_q} is irreducible as a q-\mathcal{D}-module. Transversality to the Borel subgroup prevents the existence of non-trivial sub-q-\mathcal{D}-modules.
heading: Conjecture
